subject: Pre-QBR: Launch cadence & outstanding engineering risks
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-QBR: Launch cadence & outstanding engineering risks

Team —

As we prepare the QBR deck next week I want a concise, prioritized view of anything that could materially change the launch timeline or our commitments to Acero Labs. Please treat this as the single-source preflight: I attached a running risk register and the preflight checklist.

What I need by EOD Thursday (4/15):
- Short status per milestone (On track / At risk / Blocked) with owners
- Top 3 risks that would change the launch date and proposed mitigations (owner + ETA for mitigation)
- Any ask for executive decisions (credits, scope cuts, SLA exceptions)

Initial focus areas I care about:
- API stability for streaming endpoints (customer-facing)
- Model variant performance at P99 latency at 4k seqs
- Infra capacity for Dedicated pools and canary plan

Attachments: 2027-04-10_preflight-risk_register.xlsx, 2027-04-10_preflight-checklist.pdf

I’ll consolidate into the QBR appendix and want a 30-minute pre-QBR sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT to finalize slides.

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 11:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: Launch cadence & outstanding engineering risks

Vivek —

Thanks for the note. Product status (short):
- Feature set: Core surface (generation + chat + rerank) is functionally complete; acceptance tests in progress. Status: At risk (2-day slippage on acceptance). Owner: Laura.
- Customer flows: Acero-specific templates need one API tweak (header propagation). Status: Blocked until eng change deployed. Owner: Jordan.
- Docs & support playbook: Draft ready, needs finalization after one more round of test cases. Status: On track. Owner: Priya (not in thread).

Top 3 risks we see: 
1) API header issue for Acero templates — current workaround adds latency and complexity for their infra. Impact: Could delay their go-live by 2 weeks. Mitigation: Fast-track header propagation fix + test plan; ask eng for hotfix patch by 4/13. (Owner: Jordan)
2) Model quality regression on long sequences — failing 3 internal evals for the 4k path. Impact: Might require pinning to older model variant (cost + perf tradeoff). Mitigation: Run targeted evals, prepare fallback messaging; product decision required if rollback is necessary. (Owner: Laura)
3) Billing/ingestion edge-case uncovered by Acero — need payment flow validation in staging. Impact: contract acceptance risk. Mitigation: Coordinate CS + payments to validate sandbox. (Owner: Sales/CS)

I've attached a short slide (tab in the risk register) with acceptance criteria and the recommended severity for QBR.

Cheers,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: risk_register.xlsx (sheet: product_risks)]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 12:20:37 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: Launch cadence & outstanding engineering risks

On Sat, Apr 10, 2027 at 11:02 AM Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:
> Vivek —
> 
> Thanks for the note. Product status (short):
> - Feature set: Core surface (generation + chat + rerank) is functionally complete; acceptance tests in progress. Status: At risk (2-day slippage on acceptance). Owner: Laura.

Short update from Eng:
- Header propagation hotfix: We can deliver a patch for the header issue by EOD 4/12 if we reprioritize the sprint (move non-critical infra tickets). Impact: small scope shift; requires QA signoff.
- Model regression on 4k seqs: Root cause appears to be a new tokenization edge-case combined with recent kernel optimization. We can do one of: (A) revert kernel change for the 4k path (fast, may increase cost 6%), (B) apply a targeted fix to tokenization (est. 4 dev-days), or (C) gate 4k customers onto a pinned variant with a communication plan. Recommendation: temporary revert + targeted fix in next sprint.
- Timeline: If we take (A) + hotfix, we stay within current launch window. If we do (B) only, +3–4 business days.

Mitigations I’m proposing now:
1) Reprioritize sprint to push header fix and the rollback work today (4/10).
2) Prep a pinned model variant artifact and rollout playbook for canary (eng + product + cs).
3) Extra QA slot tomorrow to validate both hotfix and model rollback at scale (requesting additional infra canary capacity).

I added estimated ETA lines to the risk register (column: eng_eta).

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:05:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: Launch cadence & outstanding engineering risks

Jordan / team —

Infra notes:
- Canary capacity: We can provision an extra Dedicated pool for canaries for the weekend but it will burn ~$7.5k in on-demand GPU hours if we do full-load validation. Recommend targeted load tests at 20% traffic to validate correctness, not full perf.
- Rollback plan: infra side is prepared to wire traffic splits and automated fallbacks; needs the pinned artifact and the routing policy (json) from eng.
- Monitoring: I will add temporary P99 tracing hooks and increase retention for telemetry for 72 hours around the tests.

Cost ask: If execs want full-load perf validation we need approval for up to $15k incremental spend (one-time). If product accepts targeted tests + staged canary we can avoid that.

Happy to run the canary tomorrow morning once Jordan’s team produces the artifact.

-Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:10:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: Launch cadence & outstanding engineering risks

Thanks — good, concrete updates. Quick summary and actions (owners):

1) Header propagation fix — Jordan / Eng to push hotfix by EOD 4/12. Laura to confirm acceptance criteria; Michael to run targeted 20% canary on 4/13 AM. (Owners: Jordan / Laura / Michael)
2) Model 4k regression — Jordan to revert kernel change for 4k path (short-term) + schedule tokenization fix in next sprint. Prepare pinned variant and customer communication. Decision if rollback impacts cost to be flagged to me by 4/14. (Owner: Jordan; Product: Laura)
3) Billing sandbox validation — Laura to coordinate CS and payments; report by 4/14. (Owner: Laura)
4) Exec cost ask — Michael to prepare a $15k one-time approval note if full perf validation is requested; otherwise we’ll follow the targeted test plan. (Owner: Michael)

I’ll fold this into the QBR appendix and include a single-slide RAG table. Please update the drive deck at the link below by 9am PT Monday with the final one-slide state and mitigation status.

Pre-QBR sync: Tomorrow 10:00am PT (30 min). Invite sent.

Drive deck: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1preflight_QBR_2027

If anything changes overnight ping me on Slack.

—Vivek
